rows.description: A teenager left outside a clique sees its members excuse each other while judging him harshly. Being the outsider shows how unfair loyalty can feel.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student notices that jobs, help and trust flow toward people from the same region or college. Naming the pattern is the first step toward being fair to everyone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A wise colleague uses clear criteria, seeks out people unlike herself, and checks whether she would make the same call if the person belonged to her own group.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child believes the kid who got punished must have done something bad, because fairness feels like the rule of the world. Unlucky events seem deserved.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager says a classmate who was bullied or robbed must have provoked it. Blaming the victim protects the comfort of believing he is safe.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student who suffers illness, failure or harassment meets people who say he must have done something to deserve it. It adds shame to pain and pushes him into silence.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A mature person accepts that bad things happen to good people, supports the sufferer, and still works for fairness where she can.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child who stumbles or gives a wrong answer believes the whole class saw and will remember. Most others were busy with their own worries.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager with a pimple or an unfashionable bag is sure everyone stares and judges, and avoids school events. The audience is far smaller than imagined.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Speaking up in class or interviews [Actor]
rows.description: A student stays quiet fearing a small slip will be remembered for weeks, while classmates barely notice or forget by evening.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
